summary: Closed the core finding's last scope gap by building and requesting the retained run of a three-node generalization. The probe (draft core_gap_three_nodes.rs, hosted in the runtime crate's test target only because it needs nothing from the actor layer) hand-drives three real OmniPaxos instances one node at a time — tick, drain, deliver — so heartbeat rounds stay aligned. Four harness defects were found and fixed on the way, each visible in the local output: the simulator's node set and its builder had to be generalized (the builder still assumed two nodes, which made node 3 fail validation), the message-kind match had to compile without the async_runtime feature, the election predicate had to accept a majority rather than every node, and the drop rule had to become a budget rather than dropping a single receipt — with only one drop the three-node cluster decided anyway because the leader needed just one follower, which is exactly the scope point; the environment assertion also miscounted AcceptDecide because one proposal produces one per promised follower. Locally all three cases now pass: `three_node_lost_accepteds_window` {produced BLE:2025, Prepare:2, Promise:2, AcceptSync:2, Accepted:4, AcceptDecide:2; dropped Accepted:2; after_drop Accepted:1, BLE:2001; leader_decided_idx 0; both followers accepted_idx 1 and holding the entry Undecided} shows the gap at three nodes, and `three_node_later_proposal_repairs` {steps_until_decided 1} shows the only repair, beside the unchanged two-node cases. The receipt will confirm or refute the generalization; if it is green, the recorded limit 'only the 2-node configuration was probed' is replaced by a measurement spanning both sizes, with the fault assumption stated (two lost receipts, i.e. exactly what the write quorum still needed).
